newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices ease on weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices ease on weather forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were dragged lower Monday by a weakening weather-related demand across most of the U.S. and the absence of some traders, market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average were down three cents to $2.25-2.28 per mmBtu, with Transco quoted mostly in the high-$2.20s.
Cooler-than-normal weather in parts of Texas also put some downward pressure on those pipes. Most south Texas deals were reported done around $2.15, down four cents from Friday.
Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line began Saturday. The work will cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd from May 14-19, with 400 mmcfd still cut from May 20-22.
On Transco at the New York city-gate, prices slipped a couple of cents to the low-$2.50s.

Temperatures throughout the Northeast are expected to drop to slightly below normal Tuesday but then quickly return to seasonable levels by midweek and continue into the weekend, Weather Services Corp said.
Appalachian prices also fell about two cents to $2.42-2.45 on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where much below-normal temperatures have arrived, prices retreated three cents to about $2.02-2.04.
Chicago and Detroit city-gate values, however, held in the low-$2.30s and about $2.40, respectively. Traders blamed the support on a steady storage injection demand.
In west Texas, Permian prices dropped five cents to the mid-to-high $1.90s, while at Waha gas sold mostly at $2.04-2.05.

Trading was fairly quiet at the southern California border due to the Santa Fe gas conference, but continued heat in the Southwest attracted some buyers to the marketplace. As a result, prices gained about four cents to about $2.15.
